key_findings.finding: The primary study is Yang et al., “Tissue factor induces VEGF expression via activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway in ARPE-19 cells” (Molecular Vision, 2016; PMID 27499609). It studied CoCl2-induced chemical hypoxia in human ARPE-19 cells; TF rose with HIF-1α/VEGF, and TF overexpression versus silencing increased versus decreased VEGF expression.

source_tools.relevance: Primary paper abstract and results preview describing model, TF manipulation, and VEGF outcomes

key_findings.finding: The paper supports Wnt/β-catenin involvement but not definitive mediation: it measured pathway-associated phosphorylated GSK3β and β-catenin by Western blot and reports that IWR-1-endo pharmacological Wnt disruption inhibited TF-overexpression effects. This inhibitor reversal supports pathway dependence, but the accessible evidence does not show a genetic rescue/epistasis test establishing that canonical Wnt/β-catenin specifically mediates the TF-to-VEGF effect.

source_tools.relevance: Methods and abstract results report pathway protein assays and IWR-1-endo inhibition
